items.title: 61539_Butter Jackson oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee discusses Erskine Hawkins' role in the band and the recording of 'Tuxedo Junction' from a historical/observational perspective, referring to him as 'he' and describing his playing style, but does not claim a personal relationship, collaboration, or direct interaction.

ctx.x: He was the owner of the Savoy Ballroom. So he liked the band and he seen how Erskine was a high note trumpet player and he was a feature man in the band, so he put him in front of the band when he signed the band up, and he started calling Erskine Hawkins the Gabes, you see.
And that was his nemesis from then on, right?
